about: The lines a Windows smoke report (RECUT_SMOKE=1, electron/main.ts runSmoke) must contain, in one list for both
Windows smoke checks so they cannot drift apart (issue #170): mode 'installer' is the unpacked installer build
(.github/workflows/windows.yml, installer job, 'Smoke-test the unpacked app'); mode 'launcher' is a run from source
by 'Start ReCut.cmd -Smoke' (scripts/windows/start-recut.ps1, the launcher job). scripts/check-smoke.mjs applies it.
Both modes require the speech-to-text engine and OCR: -Smoke runs only in CI, whose runner has CMake and Visual
Studio C++, so a launcher run that skipped or failed the engine fails (a double-click start without the tools still
Each required entry gives a JavaScript regular expression per mode, matched case-insensitively against each line of
the report; an entry without a pattern for a mode is not required in that mode. 'forbidden' is matched
case-sensitively against each line and fails the check wherever it matches. Patterns are JSON strings, so a regex
backslash is written twice (and a literal Windows backslash four times).
tests/unit/launcher-parity.test.ts checks this file against real reports of both modes.

required.what: the recut-media:// protocol serves a byte range
FFmpeg encodes a generated clip and ffprobe reads it back
FFmpeg comes from the package's resources\ffmpeg (a run from source may use an FFmpeg on PATH instead: start-recut.ps1 downloads one only when none is installed)
the OCR worker starts and loads the Tesseract core (from app.asar.unpacked when packaged, from dist\electron\ocr when run from source)
the speech-to-text engine resources\whisper\whisper-cli.exe runs (--version, no model needed)
the window loads and React mounts the layout
